gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the only named head-to-head test of a Rexing 4-channel cam with side cameras (The Smart Home Hookup's 13-camera test, Rexing R4-RD) called its image the tester's least favourite and measured its parking mode at 0.4 Wh over 30 minutes. ChatGPT's top picks are Rexing R4 Pro and R4, and no named reviewer has tested either.
standout_why: Compared against Dashlore (cited) and Car and Driver (cited). Dashlore's guide says every spec comes from maker pages and it does no lab or road testing. It covers only the Vantrue N5S as a 4-channel cam and never mentions Rexing, REDTIGER or Botslab. Car and Driver blocks this agent's fetch tool, so its page could not be read. Judging by ChatGPT's own summary, Car and Driver names the N5S best four-channel, and ChatGPT cites no Rexing test from it. The uncited top results either did not render (Tom's Guide, TechRadar) or were not opened. ChatGPT already says the N5S's side views are cabin cameras, so the Digital Camera World finding below only adds a named observation to that point.
decides: This argues against ChatGPT's top pick. No named reviewer has measured or tested the Rexing R4 Pro or R4. The one named head-to-head test of a Rexing 4-channel cam with side cameras (R4-RD) put its image at the bottom. For a shopper who wants exterior side coverage, the side-camera Rexing and Botslab models stay unproven or weak in named tests. The Vantrue N5S does best on named day-video ratings, but its own reviewer says it sees little through the side windows, especially at night. So the N5S stays our pick for overall image quality, with a clear warning that it does not really cover the sides.

findings.label: Parking-mode energy use, measured
findings.value: 0.4 Wh in 30 minutes (works out to about 0.8 W average)
findings.source_title: Best Dashcams 2025 – The Clear Winner After Testing 13 Models (The Smart Home Hookup)
findings.note: Article dated 2025-12-19. The tester measured each camera's parking modes over a 30-minute run. 0.4 Wh ÷ 0.5 h = 0.8 W is my arithmetic. The R4-RD is the 4-channel Rexing with side cameras and a built-in 360° parking monitor. It is a different model from the R4 and R4 Pro that ChatGPT recommended.

findings.label: Image quality in a head-to-head test
findings.value: Called 'my least favorite image' in Round 2; sits near the bottom of the article's final 'The Rest' ranking
findings.source_title: Best Dashcams 2025 – The Clear Winner After Testing 13 Models (The Smart Home Hookup)
findings.note: Cameras were compared in rounds of four on day and night video, field of view, and license plates captured stationary, moving and passing at speed. In the same test, Vantrue N4 Pro S averaged rank 1.33 in Round 3 and 1.5 in Round 4, and was called 'the king of nighttime video quality'. The R4-RD was listed at $229.

findings.label: Side coverage through the cabin cameras, hands-on
findings.value: 'exterior coverage from the cabin cameras isn't great'; at night 'very little will be visible through the car's side windows'
findings.source_title: Vantrue Nexus 5S (N5S) dash cam review – an all-round four-camera solution (Digital Camera World, Ben Andrews)
findings.note: Published 2026-02-12. This is an observation, not a number. Ben Andrews also found front plates good for cars directly ahead, and passing plates at night 'just about visible when you freeze the video'. Cabin cameras on infrared are 'noticeably softer'. He did not test parking mode.

findings.label: Recording storage use, measured by an owner
findings.value: About 1 GB per 3-minute loop with all four cameras at top resolution, or about 6 hours on a 128 GB card
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue Nexus 5S (DashCamTalk forum, member EricSan)
findings.note: Posted 2025-09-09 after a real drive. In the same thread, EricSan measured supercapacitor run-on after power loss at 3–4 s (2025-09-04). DashCamTalk's spec table lists bitrates of 14.3 Mbps front and 9.8 Mbps rear, but those are listed specs, not measurements.

findings.label: DashCamTalk ratings
findings.value: Overall 7.0/10; day video 8; night video 6; reliability 7
findings.note: DashCamTalk does not say how it scores. The only exception is the app score (8.3), which comes from app-store ratings. Use for side-by-side comparison only.

findings.label: DashCamTalk ratings
findings.value: Overall 6.7/10; day video 7; night video 6; reliability 6

Its spec table lists a 2560×1440 IMX675 front camera at 16 Mbps and three 1080p cameras at 10 Mbps, all from specs. The rear and second cabin cameras are cabin- or rear-facing, not side cameras.
